review.summary:
changes_needed
Managed Agents handler exits on tool pauses before work finishes.
Restart recovery misses unresolved calls because streaming does not replay history.
Tool-runner answer incorrectly says a text-only response requires exiting the runner.
Checks: 29 tests passed; link checker: bad 0.

findings.checklist_item: Accuracy: code sketches do what the text says.
findings.title: Continue handling events after a custom-tool pause
findings.claim: The unconditional break treats requires_action as completion. That idle event can arrive after the handler has already sent its tool result, causing it to disconnect before subsequent work finishes.
findings.evidence: Executing the extracted sketch with custom call 1, requires_action, custom call 2, end_turn sent only call 1's result. The [session-event documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming) explicitly says the requires_action event still appears after an immediate result.
findings.proposed_change: Branch on stop_reason.type: continue across resolved tool pauses, route outstanding confirmations to their handler, and record budget termination separately. Verify that two custom calls separated by requires_action both receive results.

findings.checklist_item: Accuracy: code sketches and worked answers implement the promised resumability.
findings.title: Recover unresolved calls from history before tailing live events
findings.claim: Persisting done_store does not implement the promised restart recovery. If the handler dies after inserting a result but before sending it, reopening the sketch's stream will not deliver the old call again.
findings.evidence: The [reconnect documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming) says streams deliver only new events and requires combining streaming with event history. The sketch reads no history to dispatch unresolved calls.
findings.proposed_change: Open the stream, reconcile pending calls from persisted event history, resend stored results, then tail live events with overlap deduplication. Test a restart between inserting and sending the result.

findings.checklist_item: Accuracy: framework behavior and worked answers.
findings.title: Correct the tool runner's text-only response handling
findings.claim: The runner does not necessarily exit before the caller can respond to a text-only message. The answer incorrectly presents an outer loop as necessary.
findings.evidence: The [Tool Runner advanced-usage documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-runner) says the response is yielded before the termination check. Modifying message history inside that iteration bypasses automatic handling and continues with the supplied history.
findings.proposed_change: Explain that the caller can append the assistant response and a 'Not submitted yet' user message inside the existing iteration, retaining max_iterations=12. Add a dated correction if the source email made the original claim. Verify continuation after a stubbed text-only response.

findings.checklist_item: Accuracy: workspace limits and their operational consequences.
findings.title: Separate workspaces do not reserve production throughput
findings.claim: Creating separate workspaces alone does not prevent an eval sweep from consuming production's available throughput. Both remain subject to the shared organization limit. The glossary's Workspace entry repeats this guarantee.
findings.evidence: The [official rate-limit documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits) says unset workspace limits match the organization's limit and organization-wide limits always apply. It recommends lower workspace caps to protect other workspaces.
findings.proposed_change: Say to separate workspaces and explicitly cap nonproduction traffic below the shared organization limit, leaving capacity for production. Update the glossary too, and explain the case where uncapped eval traffic exhausts the shared limit.

findings.checklist_item: Accuracy: distinguish defaults from fixed product limits.
findings.title: Qualify AgentCore's configurable idle timeout
findings.claim: The lesson presents 15 minutes idle as an unavoidable termination boundary. It is a configurable default. The fixed-boundary wording repeats in the API table, common mistakes and glossary.
findings.evidence: AWS's [lifecycle-settings documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-lifecycle-settings.html) identifies idleRuntimeSessionTimeout as configurable, defaulting to 900 seconds, with a range of 60–28,800 seconds for microVM runtimes.
findings.proposed_change: Describe 15 minutes as the default idle timeout and distinguish it from the microVM lifetime ceiling. Put the configuration identifier and limits in the API table; qualify the repeated statements while retaining the warning about ephemeral state.

findings.checklist_item: Accuracy: exercise commands perform the stated check.
findings.title: Make the seam-check command search directories recursively
findings.claim: grep -l does not search directory contents without a recursive option, so this command cannot list the seam violations requested.
findings.evidence: Running the command returned exit code 2 and 'grep: tools/: Is a directory'. The other two exercise directories are absent from this notes repository; creating them would still require recursive searching.
findings.proposed_change: Use grep -RlE 'anthropic|langgraph' tools/ guards/ evals/ in the reader's implementation. Verify that it finds a framework import in a nested file, and inspect matches to distinguish imports from harmless text.

findings.checklist_item: Lesson template: worked answers answer the exercise as set.
findings.title: Identify the missing implementation portions of the worked answers
findings.claim: The integrative answer addresses only the planted faults and reversal question. It omits the deployment design, code and manifest requested in steps 1–6. Similarly, 9.5 requests implementations of provenance recovery and a durable done store, but its answer supplies only prose.
findings.evidence: Lines 942–949 request a one-page design and about 80 lines of code; lines 961–969 provide three fault outcomes and a paragraph. Line 699 requests about 20 lines of implementation, while lines 715–719 only describe its behavior.
findings.proposed_change: Fill these implementation portions from the source answers where available. If the emails do not supply them, explicitly label the answers as partial and identify the unanswered parts instead of marking the entire exercise answered.
